text:
mira: Heads-up — saw a reproducible pattern on canary with AWQ act-quant enabled where some requests return truncated or garbled continuations. started after we bumped group_size to 64 for perf.
jamal: details? which model / config? any logs?
mira: model: raven-13b-open-adapt, awq config: actq=per_group, actq_bits=4, group_size=64, kv_cache_prefetch=true. repro load: continuous streaming via dedicated pool. logs show repeated: `WARN awq: sample_shed detected, drop_count=3` and some `kv_cache index mismatch` lines.
kevin: "sample_shed" sounds like our batcher dropping items under backpressure. could be alignment bug where group partitioning mislabels sequences, esp with act-quant present.
eva: can you paste the exact log snippet? also which commit of runner/runtime?
mira: here's the snippet:

```
2026-03-18T14:12:33Z WARN awq: sample_shed batch_id=4821 drop_idx=[2,5] reason=kv_mismatch
2026-03-18T14:12:33Z ERROR serve: decode_assertion failed token_seq_len=128 kv_len=120
2026-03-18T14:12:34Z INFO awq: fallback to fp8 variant model=raven-13b-open-adapt:v2
```

mira: runner hash: a3f5c2e, runtime: 2.9.1, serving config was patched yesterday with continuous batching optimizations.
jamal: quick theory: AWQ group_size is changing how we pack activations into the fused kernels. act quant introduces per-group scaling tables — if batcher shuffles sample ordering between kernel calls, table lookup could be mismatched.
kevin: agree. two quick repros: 1) run heavy streaming write to group_size=64 with actq on, 2) same with group_size=32 or actq disabled. compare failure rates.
eva: i spun up a tiny canary: group_size=64 + actq on -> 12/1000 requests garbled. group_size=32 + actq on -> 0/1000. actq off + group_size=64 -> 1/1000. so looks strongly correlated to group_size and actq interaction.
mira: thanks — that matches our prod mirrors. any cheap mitigation we can flip now?
kevin: short-term: autoswitch rule in router: if model=raven-13b-open-adapt and actq enabled and group_size>=48, route to fp8 variant. quick fix via console.
jamal: can we instead force group_size override lower for this model on Dedicated pools? preserving awq perf but avoiding regression.
eva: doing that now for staging. also kicking off a small perf reg test to estimate latency impact. will report.

[~10m later]
eva: result: forcing group_size=32 increases p50 latency by 6% but reduces token cost by similar? accuracy on eval harness improved — perplexity drop ~0.9. so tradeoff looks fine while we debug.
mira: good. next: bisect kernel path that touches act-quant table indexing. @kevin can you open a bisect PR and include a small test that locks group boundary behavior?
kevin: on it. i'll add a deterministic micro-batch unit test that simulates shuffled ordering and validates scale indices.
jamal: also can we add an eval-driven regression alert: when actq enabled and group_size >= 48, create a health score and page if degradation > 0.5% on any safety/qa metric.
mira: yes please. @eval-bot can you add a continuous check against our piqa/hellaswag prompt-sets for this model? we need an automated smoke.
eval-bot: ack — scheduling hourly runs for raven-13b-open-adapt with both awq and fp8 variants. will post diffs to #eng-ml-results.
deploy-bot: canary rollback rule ready — will automatically fallback to fp8 variant if >2% degraded responses in 5m window.
kevin: final note: strange that sample_shed logs exist; need to audit batcher code path for in-flight mutation of sample metadata. might be separate from actq but they combine badly. i'll take that audit.
mira: thanks all. immediate action items: (1) eva forces group_size=32 in staging & rotates canary (2) kevin bisect + unit test (3) jamal creates alert + router rule change to route to fp8 when conditions met (4) eval-bot start hourly checks.
kevin: will update thread with PR link and test results.
jamal: adding a tiny debug metric: `awq.group_mismatch_rate` to help triage.
mira: nice. saving logs to /infra/awq/debug/2799987654.tar.gz and will attach to the bisect PR.
kevin: noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
